extraction.name: CIFAR-10
extraction.description: CIFAR-10 is among the most widely used datasets in machine learning, facilitating thousands of research projects per year. The paper focuses on developing fast training methods for this dataset.
extraction.creator: Krizhevsky et al.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper uses the CIFAR-10 dataset, which is a pre-existing dataset containing 60,000 32x32 color images divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images. The paper does not describe original data collection as it reuses this existing dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CIFAR-10 dataset consisting of 60,000 32x32 color images labeled as one of ten classes, with 50,000 training images and 10,000 validation images
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training neural networks for image classification research, accelerating machine learning experiments, and benchmarking training speed on CIFAR-10. The methods are designed for scenarios requiring different accuracy levels (94%, 95%, and 96%).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Code is released as the airbench Python package on GitHub at https://github.com/KellerJordan/cifar10-airbench. Multiple variants are provided (airbench94_compiled.py, airbench94.py, airbench95.py, airbench96.py).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data augmentation using derandomized horizontal flipping (alternating flip), 2-pixel random translation with reflection padding, and label smoothing at rate 0.2. Test-time augmentation using horizontal flipping and multi-crop evaluation with six augmented views (unmodified, up-left translation, down-right translation, and mirrored versions) with weighted averaging (0.25 for untranslated, 0.125 for translated views). Random reshuffling of training data across epochs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Patch-whitening initialization applied to first convolutional layer using eigenvectors of covariance matrix of 2x2 patches across training distribution to achieve identity covariance matrix output.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: CIFAR-10 is among the most widely used datasets in machine learning, facilitating thousands of research projects per year. To accelerate research and reduce the cost of experiments, we introduce training methods for CIFAR-10 which reach 94% accuracy in 3.29 seconds, 95% in 10.4 seconds, and 96% in 46.3 seconds

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Our code is released at https://github.com/KellerJordan/cifar10-airbench... It is released as the airbench Python package.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: For data augmentation we use random horizontal flipping alongside 2-pixel random translation. For translation we use reflection padding (Zagoruyko & Komodakis, 2016) which we found to be better than zero-padding... we use a label smoothing rate of 0.2... To generate predictions, we run the trained network on six augmented views of each test image: the unmodified input, a version which is translated up-and-to-the-left by one pixel, a version which is translated down-and-to-the-right by one pixel, and the mirrored versions of all three. Predictions are made using a weighted average of all six outputs, where the two views of the untranslated image are weighted by 0.25 each, and the remaining four views are weighted by 0.125 each... we propose a derandomized variant of horizontal flipping augmentation... random reshuffling leads to all N unique examples being seen every epoch.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Following Page (2019); tysam-code (2023) we initialize the first convolutional layer as a patch-whitening transformation. The layer is a 2x2 convolution with 24 channels. Following tysam-code (2023) the first 12 filters are initialized as the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix of 2x2 patches across the training distribution, so that their outputs have identity covariance matrix.
